title: The Socratic Method
alternate_titles: The Socratic Method: A Practitioner's Handbook

contents: What the Socratic method is and where it came from
The elements of the method, step by step, with examples from Plato's dialogues
The elenchus: testing principles for consistency
Ignorance, aporia, and the double meaning of knowing you don't know
Socratic ethics: the method as patience, inquiry, humility, and doubt
The method against the habits of modern discourse

audiences: Readers who want to think and argue more carefully
Teachers, lawyers, and coaches who work by questioning
Readers of Stoicism looking for its Socratic roots
Anyone exhausted by the quality of modern argument

sources.title: The Socratic Method
sources.supports: Title, author, publication dates, ISBNs, 264 pages, formats, the publisher's description (method as technique and ethic; hundreds of classical quotations; chapters on Socratic Ethics, Ignorance, Testing Principles, Socrates and the Stoics), and attributed review quotes.
sources.limitations: Publisher copy; authoritative for facts, promotional for quality.

sources.title: George F. Will on The Socratic Method
sources.author_or_publisher: The Washington Post (quoted by the publisher)
sources.supports: Independent columnist's assessment: the method decelerates reasoning and is an antidote to social pandemics of our day.
sources.limitations: Accessed via publisher-quoted excerpts rather than the original column.

sources.title: Ward Farnsworth, The Socratic Method: A Practitioner's Handbook
sources.supports: Independent bibliographic confirmation and the book's registration in the philosophy literature index.

sources.title: Ward Farnsworth on the Socratic Method
sources.supports: The author's own account of the book's aims and the method's relevance to modern discourse.

sources.title: You Must Change Your Writing Style: Ward Farnsworth's Guidebooks
sources.supports: Independent literary assessment of Farnsworth's handbook method: quotation-anthology structure, clarity, and the genre's limits.
sources.limitations: Assesses the author's series; the Socratic volume shares the method.

sources.title: The Socratic Method: A Practitioner's Handbook
sources.supports: Warm reader reception with recurring notes: exceptional clarity, and some readers wanting more practice drills than the handbook label implies.

workflow.coverage_notes: Built from the publisher record, independent professional commentary, the author's interviews, and reader reception; chapter-level claims follow the publisher's own chapter list and the author's account.
next_steps: Optional: verify the dialogue-by-dialogue examples against a full copy to raise coverage.
